entities.name: PMID:27506669
observations: Pooled analysis of 120 stage II–III oesophageal cancer patients receiving curative-intent chemoradiation; compared pretreatment FACT-E/ECS with ECOG for overall-survival discrimination.
Pretreatment FACT-E and ECS predicted overall survival, whereas ECOG did not; AUCs were 0.63, 0.69, and 0.56, respectively.

entities.name: PMID:18081735
observations: Prospective multicentre study of 96 patients with incurable oesophageal or gastro-oesophageal-junction cancer; assessed EORTC QLQ-C30/QLQ-OES18 and Karnofsky Index.
Physical functioning, fatigue, and reflux added prognostic information beyond M-stage, but formal discrimination superiority over Karnofsky was not reported.

entities.name: QoL versus ECOG discrimination
observations: In 120 stage II–III patients, pretreatment ECS had AUC 0.69 (95% CI 0.60–0.79), FACT-E had AUC 0.63 (0.52–0.73), and ECOG had AUC 0.56 (0.45–0.66) for survival discrimination.
FACT-E and ECS were independently associated with overall survival, while ECOG was not.

entities.name: EORTC incremental prognosis
observations: In 96 incurable oesophageal or gastro-oesophageal-junction cancer patients, physical functioning, fatigue, and reflux added prognostic information beyond M-stage.
The study did not report formal AUC, C-statistic, or nested-model superiority of QLQ-C30/QLQ-OES18 over Karnofsky.
